MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 12, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Doug Stewart and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Rob DuBoux, Interim City
  Manager; Christopher Smith, Assistant City Manager; Richard Rojas, Deputy City
  Manager; Frances Arricale, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Community Development
  Director; Susan Duerias, Public Safety Director; Parker Davis, Media. Technician; Greg
  Kajszo, Assistant to the City Manager Christina Murioz, Deputy City Clerk; Chris Orosz,
  Recreation Manager; and Nadia Fahoum, Associate Engineer.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Riggins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  December 23, 2025.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda, continuing Item No. 1.B.6. to a date uncertain. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment. As there were no public
  speakers present for the Consent Calendar, the Mayor returned the matter to the

1  table for discussion.

  Item Nos. 1.B.4., 1.B.5., and 1.B.10. were pulled by the Council.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 2 of 12

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 1.B.4., 1.B.5., 1.B.10. The
  motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  77431-77649 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 781 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $4,018,338.14. City of Malibu payroll check number 5542-5545 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $973,934.48.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 23, 2025 Regular
  Meeting.
  7.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with Transtech Engineers,
  Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1
  to the Professional Services Agreement with Transtech Engineers, Inc.
  (Transtech) to provide On-Call Civil Engineering Services.
  8.  Acceptance of Emergency Guardrail Repair Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept Public Works agreement with Stacy and
  Witbeck, Inc. for emergency guardrail repairs in order to immediately
  preserve public safety; and 2) Authorize the Public Works Director to
  submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.
  9.  Bailment Agreement with the County of Los Angeles
  Recommended Action: Authorize the City Manager to execute a bailment
  agreement with the County of Los Angeles to allow the Sheriff's
  Department to use a new City vehicle for the Volunteers on Patrol program.
  11.  Facility Fee Waiver Policy
  Recommended Action: Adopt City Council Policy #53 Facility Fee
  Waiver.
  12.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding the Franklin Fire
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 26-03, extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency in response to the Franklin
  Fire.
  13.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding the Palisades Fire
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 3 of 12

  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 26-04, extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency in response to the
  Palisades Fire.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  6.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with Kimley-Horn and
  Associates, Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1
  to Professional Services Agreement with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc.
  for additional engineering design services and support during construction
  of the Pacific Coast Highway Quick Build Roundabout project in the
  amount $198,550, for a new total not to exceed in the amount $477,926.

  This item was continued to a date uncertain upon approval of the agenda.

  4.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding Conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 26-02 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency related to the increase of
  reckless and illegal driving on Pacific Coast Highway and directing staff to
  coordinate efforts with other governmental agencies to increase attention
  and create programs to reduce the risk and danger associated with Pacific
  Coast Highway in the City:

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded
  a motion to adopt Resolution No. 26-02 extending the declaration of the
  existence of a local emergency related to the increase of reckless and illegal
  driving on Pacific Coast Highway and directing staff to coordinate efforts
  with other governmental agencies to increase attention and create programs
  to reduce the risk and danger associated with Pacific Coast Highway in the
  City. The motion carried unanimously.

  5.  Rejection of Bids for the Encinal Canyon Road 60-Inch Storm Drain
  Repairs Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Reject all bids received for the Encinal Canyon
  Road 60-Inch Storm Drain Repairs Project (Project), Specification No.
  2113; and 2) direct staff to revise scope of work required to repair the storm
  drain on Emilia! Canyon Road and rebid the Project.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a
  motion to: 1) reject all bids received for the Encinal Canyon Road 60-Inch
  Storm Drain Repairs Project (Project), Specification No. 2113; and 2) direct
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 4 of 12

  staff to revise scope of work required to repair the storm drain on Encinal
  Canyon Road and rebid the Project. The motion carried unanimously.

  10.  Termination of the Declaration of a Local Emergency
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 26-01 terminating the
  declaration of local emergency as a result of the risk of fires associated with
  individuals engaged in unpermitted camping.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Uhring second a
  motion to take no action on the termination of the Declaration of a Local
  Emergency as a result of the risk of fires associated with individuals
  engaged in unpermitted camping and acknowledge the state of emergency
  would lapse unless renewed pursuant to Government Code Section 8630.
  The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Interim City Manager DuBoux thanked the Council for the opportunity to serve and
  assist with the City Manager transition. He discussed significant rainfall over the
  holidays and commended the Public Works Maintenance crews for their work on
  Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve, and New Year's Day to keep
  roads open. He provided an update regarding the permanent Skatepark project
  timeline. He announced upcoming rebuild workshops, the Pacific Coast Highway
  (PCH) signal synchronization ribbon cutting, and that the PCH signal
  synchronization project had won the Public Works' Project of the Year award. He
  announced the closure of City Hall for Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

  In response to Mayor Riggins, Community Development Director Bundy clarified
  that the upcoming Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) workshop
  would be virtual.

  Community Development Director Bundy presented an update on fire rebuild
  statistics and projects under construction.

  The Council directed questions to Community Development Director Bundy.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein requested consensus to bring back an item for the City
  to investigate how many rebuild home permits had been issued by the City of Los
  Angeles, including through a Public Records Act request if necessary.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 5 of 12

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item at the January 26,
  2025 meeting with information regarding City of Los Angeles rebuilding permit
  statistics and to consider providing further direction to staff.

  The Council directed further questions to Community Development Director
  Bundy.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, presented the
  December 2025 crime statistics. He discussed 2026 safety goals including PCH
  safety, and rebuilding safety with ongoing construction projects. He encouraged
  individuals with security cameras to register with the Real Time Crime Center.

  The Council directed questions to Sergeant Soderlund.

  In response to the Council, Public Safety Director Duefias stated staff was preparing
  a comprehensive report on parking enforcement.

MOTION  Councilmember Conrad moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein seconded a motion
  to hear Item No. 8.A. after Item No. 4.B. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Anne K. discussed radio range in the City of Malibu and La Habra's emergency
  radio systems. She recommended prioritizing radio communication.

  Michel Shane discussed the PCH state of emergency. He proposed a new
  enforcement policy that would cause individuals speeding on PCH lose their
  license. He recommended expansion of the State's Forwarded Actions for
  Speeding Tickets (FAST) Program to include PCH in Malibu.

  Marissa Coughlan stated that two Planning Verifications sha had applied for had
  been approved and discussed the importance of expediting rebuilds to maintain
  funding and the tax base for the City and school district. She discussed FEMA
  floodplain impacts on beachfront properties and misinformation regarding fire
  rebuilds.

  Brian Merrick discussed his experience applying for his beachfront fire rebuild
  permits.

  Kevin Keegan discussed concerns that the City's strategic plan did not include
  public health goals or significant technology investment and did not sufficiently
  address emerging technologies.

  Darren Graves discussed the approved Planning Verification application for his
  family's property, and significant cost of advanced onsite wastewater treatment
  system (AOWTS) and the associated shoreline protection devices.  He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 6 of 12

  recommended an electronic plan review process and discussed miscommunications
  in the current process.

  Scott Dittrich discussed Salwa Walba's communications with Los Angeles County
  Tax Assessor Prang regarding property taxes for fire damaged properties.

  Meril May discussed safety issues near the Corral Canyon construction site,
  including maintenance of safety infrastructure such as channelizers, accidents on
  PCH, and increased concerns related to the Zuma Underpass closure.

  Nick Corey discussed open Code Enforcement case on Councilmember Uhring's
  property.

  Gary Harkness discussed Malibu Township Council's (MTC) opposition to PCH
  safety improvements. He discussed MTC formation and purpose in its early
  history. He expressed concern that the MTC no longer represented the community.

  Cici Lee discussed removal of Norfolk Pine Trees on Cross Creek Road.

  Jo Drummond discussed the year since the Palisades Fire. She discussed the limited
  number of rebuild permits that had been issued and challenges to the rebuilding
  process.

  Norm Haynie discussed long-term impacts of rains and delayed slides after the hills
  are saturated. He discussed the difference between planning and building permits
  in the development process.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Councilmember Stewart stated that the
  Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) used radios similar to those
  demonstrated by Anne K.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Community Development Director Bundy,
  Interim City Manager DuBoux, and Assistant City Manager SMith discussed the
  current plan review process and the City's plans for an electronic land management
  system.

  Councilmember Conrad requested consensus to support Los Angeles County Tax
  Assessor Prang's efforts regarding reduced property taxes for fire-damaged
  properties.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed property taxes after the Woolsey Fire and the
  way the current assessment is applied to damaged or destroyed properties.

  Councilmember Conrad requested updates on major projects like the project near
  Corral Canyon where work had been stopped.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 7 of 12

Interim City Manager DuBoux stated he could provide an update to the Council.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux explained
the purpose of temporary construction channelizers and alternative products for
long-term solutions.

Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein discussed how he had advocated for the City to take
further actions under the PCH emergency declaration.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated Caltrans
had jurisdiction over PCH and explained the limited powers of emergency
declaration and the risk of taking action without coordination with Caltrans.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux requested
anyone who sees a dangerous situation report the issue to the City Manager or
Public Works so it can be documented in the City's weekly meeting with Caltrans.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Community Development Director Bundy
stated that septic systems and seawalls were currently the responsibility of the
property owner rebuilding from the fire. She stated that Caltrans was assessing
seawalls adjoining PCH and would shore certain walls, but had not agreed to pay
for private property improvements.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Community Development Director Bundy
stated Community Development staff monitored California Coastal Commission
(CCC) agendas and met regularly with CCC staff.

Councilmember Conrad thanked the Community Services Department for the extra
hour for the senior center knitting programming.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated staff had patched damaged carpet after water damage in the multi-purpose
room, but the full carpet would be replaced in future with minimal impact to
programming.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated
Caltrans had placed protective devices in the PCH median in the fire damaged area
to prevent erosion.

In response to Mayor Riggins, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated the City had
conveyed to the County that plastic sandbags were not allowed in the City.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated the
timeline for the permanent Skatepark construction had not been finalized.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Community Services Director Riesgo
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 8 of 12

  stated staff could work with the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority
  (MRCA) to address the fire-damaged trees near Bluffs Park.

  Councilmember Stewart thanked Candace Bond for her service as Interim City
  Manager. He stated he attended the Palisades Fire remembrance event and
  discussed the impact fires have had on the City.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Interim City Manager DuBoux provided
  an update on the speed camera procurement and installation timeline.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed radio systems being used across Southern
  California and the importance of having strong towers to support the system.

  Councilmember Uhring thanked Public Works crews for keeping roads open
  through the recent rain events. He discussed options for soils testing for fire
  damaged properties. He discussed the Palisaded Fire Remembrance event. He
  stated the City had been in contact with him regarding the Code Enforcement case.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, Interim City Manager DuBoux
  discussed issues with permitting for the Zuma Beach underpass cleanup.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein discussed Anne K.'s comments regarding La Habra and
  differences between fire danger and La Habra and Malibu.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein discussed whether rebuild permitting rights travel with
  the land, and explained that planning entitlements continue with the land while
  building code provisions may differ in landslide zones.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, Community Development Director
  Bundy discussed conditions for properties in an active landslide zone to rebuild.
  She explained that one condition was that building permits could be issued to the
  owner, the owner's heirs, or authorized agents, and stated that staff was reviewing
  the implications of this provision for the sale of these properties.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein requested consensus to bring back an item to discuss
  this issue and consider a legislative solution.

  Mayor Riggins indicated support for the proposed item.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart and Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein,
  Community Development Director Bundy explained which properties fell under
  this active landslide classification and when properties in an active landslide area
  could be rebuilt with up to an additional 10%.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to discuss the
  Building Code restrictions on who can rebuild a damaged or destroyed structure in
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 9 of 12

  an active landslide zone.

  In response to Mayor Riggins, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated staff would
  bring back an item on the PCH sewer project soon.

  Mayor Riggins requested California Highway Patrol (CHP) provide a law
  enforcement update to a future City Council meeting.

  In response to Mayor Riggins, Interim City Manager DuBoux stated staff could
  bring back a more detailed update on Big Rock dewatering system.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein and Councilmember Conrad,
  Community Development Director Bundy explained that the landslide was mapped
  by the State.

  In response to Mayor Riggins, Community Development Director Bundy stated the
  City's geotechnical consultant could provide more information on the active
  landslide classification and mapping.

  Councilmember Conrad requested consensus to bring back an item to determine
  which Councilmembers can attend the Zone Captain meetings.

  Councilmember Uhring stated he would not attend future Zone Captain meetings
  to avoid a Brown Act issues.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin explained that
  because the Zone Captain meetings were City-organized meetings, a quorum of the
  Council could not attend without noticing the meeting as a special City Council
  meeting.

  Councilmember Conrad requested consensus to schedule an item related to the
  Mobilehome Park Rent regulations.

  Interim City Manager DuBoux stated staff would bring back an item on February
  9, 2026.

RECESS  At 8:08 p.m., Mayor Riggins recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:25
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

ITEM 8  COUNCIL ITEMS

  A.  Proposal for a Council Policy to Facilitate the Expeditious, Efficient and
  Economical Rebuild of all Structures in the City Destroyed or Materially Damaged
  by Wildfire, Earthquake, Flood, Landslide, Mudslide or Similar Disaster in
  Substantially the Same Location as the Destroyed or Damaged Structure and in a
  Like-for-Like Manner that Does Not Exceed 110% of the Area, Height or Bulk of
  the Structure Destroyed or Materially Damaged (a "Like-for-Like Disaster
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 10 of 12

  Rebuild"). (Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein and Councilmember Conrad) (Continued
  from December 8, 2025)
  Recommended Action: At the request of Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein and
  Councilmember Conrad, discuss and provide direction on the attached resolution.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein presented the report.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Kevin Keegan, Daniel Smith (Lea Johnson and Luis Tena deferred time
  to Daniel Smith), Darren Graves, Arno Koch (Matthew Kocher deferred time to
  Arno Koch), Scott Dittrich, Janet Fulk, Abe Roy, Brian Merrick, Marissa
  Coughlan, Jo Drummond, Tina Segel

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to schedule a workshop with the newly
  appointed City Manager Joe Irvin to discuss the proposed Council Policy to
  Facilitate the Expeditious, Efficient and Economical Rebuild of all Structures in the
  City Destroyed or Materially Damaged by Wildfire, Earthquake, Flood, Landslide,
  Mudslide or Similar Disaster.

  The Council discussed the item.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Adoption of Ordinance No. 531 - California Building Standards Code
  Recommended Action: 1) Conduct the Public Hearing; and 2) Conduct the second
  reading, unless waived, and adopt Ordinance No. 531, adopting by reference Title
  26 of the Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Building Code,
  2025 Edition; Title 27 of the Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the
  California Electrical Code, 2025 Edition; Title 28 of the Los Angeles County Code,
  incorporating the California Plumbing Code, 2025 Edition; Title 29 of the Los
  Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Mechanical Code, 2025
  Edition; Title 30 of the Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the California
  Residential Code, 2025 Edition; Title 31 of the Los Angeles County Code,
  incorporating the California Green Building Standards Code, 2025 edition; the
  California Energy Code, 2025 Edition; Title 33 of the Los Angeles County Code,
  incorporating the California Existing Building Code, 2025 Edition; the California
  Fire Code, 2025 Edition; making amendments to said codes; repealing Ordinance
  No. 503, and finding the action exempt from the California Environmental Quality
  Act.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 11 of 12

  Community Development Director Bundy presented the staff report.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Jo Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Riggins seconded a motion to adopt
  Ordinance No. 531, adopting by reference Title 26 of the Los Angeles County
  Code, incorporating the California Building Code, 2025 Edition; Title 27 of the Los
  Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Electrical Code, 2025 Edition;
  Title 28 of the Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Plumbing
  Code, 2025 Edition; Title 29 of the Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the
  California Mechanical Code, 2025 Edition; Title 30 of the Los Angeles County
  Code, incorporating the California Residential Code, 2025 Edition; Title 31 of the
  Los Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Green Building Standards
  Code, 2025 edition; the California Energy Code, 2025 Edition; Title 33 of the Los
  Angeles County Code, incorporating the California Existing Building Code, 2025
  Edition; the California Fire Code, 2025 Edition; making amendments to said codes;
  repealing Ordinance No. 503, and finding the action exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  The motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion
  to hear Item No. 6.A. after 10:30 p.m. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Request to Re-Establish a Temporary Volunteer Fire Rebuild Ambassador
  Continued from December 8, 2025)
  Recommended Action: Discuss and provide direction regarding the request to re-
  establish a Temporary Volunteer Fire Rebuild Ambassador.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to determine that the City Council would not re-establish the Temporary Volunteer
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 12, 2026
  Page 12 of 12

  Rebuild Ambassador. The motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to hear Item No. 6.B. after 10:30 p.m. The motion carried unanimously.

  B.  Receive and File Update on Malibu's Community Lands (Continued from
  December 8, 2025)
  Receive and file an update on Malibu's Community Lands, and provide direction
  to staff as appropriate.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas recommended continuing this item to the next
  available meeting.

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Mariano Shulman

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Riggins returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council continued the item to the next available meeting.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Riggins adjourned the meeting at 10:54 p.m. in memory of Darlene Dubray.

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  City of Malibu on August 24, 2026.

  BRUCE SILVE STEIN, Mayor
